summary: Pick this when the room wants a cult comedy that keeps rewarding people who love fake-band lore, tiny rock-star grievances, and endlessly quotable bits. One viewer says, "I thought it was really funny," which undersells how well it plays as shared deadpan chaos.
good_pick_if: You want deadpan band satire that gets funnier when everyone starts quoting it.
maybe_skip_if: You need a plot-heavy comedy or do not enjoy dry showbiz parody.
nearby_comps: What We Do in the Shadows

source_quotes.text: I thought it was really funny but my dad thinks it’s funnier.
I'm disappointed Letterboxd ratings don't go to 11.

summary: This is a dark, risky comedy-night pick for groups that can handle satire with real bite. The appeal is the whiplash between subject matter and absurd timing: one review calls it "brilliantly funny," while another frames it as sharp political comedy.
good_pick_if: Your group wants a fearless farce that turns discomfort into nervous laughter.
maybe_skip_if: Terrorism as comedy is a hard no for anyone watching.

source_quotes.text: Somehow I’d forgotten how brilliantly funny this is.
Possibly the finest political satire since Dr. Strangelove.

summary: A great old-Hollywood comedy pick when you want joke density, musical showmanship, and performers who keep blowing up the room. One viewer sums up the Marx Brothers energy with "These guys are out of control," which is exactly the fun.
good_pick_if: You want vintage comedy that moves from wordplay to physical mayhem fast.
maybe_skip_if: You are not in the mood for 1930s pacing or broad stage-style bits.

source_quotes.text: These guys are out of control.
I was too busy being entertained by the antics of the brothers to notice or care.

summary: Choose this for a quieter, talk-afterward movie night about friendship, ambition, and the ache of making your own life. The review phrase "how to be comfortable with being alone" catches the movie's small, deeply relatable emotional charge.
good_pick_if: You want intimate, observant drama that feels close to real adult friendship.
maybe_skip_if: You need big plot turns or a glossy comfort-watch mood.
nearby_comps: The Worst Person in the World

source_quotes.text: how to be comfortable with being alone.
captures loneliness in a society that’s so obsessed with being in love

summary: This works as a gentle crime-comedy curveball: warm, odd, and sly instead of hard-boiled. The pull is right there in "classic cinematography, noir aesthetic, subtle irony" - a playful Soviet spin on cops, cars, and moral mischief.
good_pick_if: You want an offbeat international comedy with a soft heart and sly style.
maybe_skip_if: You want fast modern pacing or broad punchline comedy.

source_quotes.text: classic cinematography, noir aesthetic, subtle irony
Soviet comedy would be a close winner.

summary: A bright, easy-to-say-yes rom-com when the room wants color, movement, and flirting that actually has a pulse. One review says it "Oozes with so much style and infectious energy," and that is the whole movie-night pitch.
good_pick_if: You want a short, lively romance with jokes, style, and instant charm.
maybe_skip_if: You dislike wide-lens visual play or very heightened rom-com energy.

source_quotes.text: Oozes with so much style and infectious energy
So charming. Vivian Oparah is a star.

summary: Go here for playful French New Wave romance where style, color, and performance matter as much as the argument. A viewer calls the fourth-wall breaks "so fun and charming," which is a useful warning and invitation in one line.
good_pick_if: You want a formally playful, colorful romance that winks at the audience.
maybe_skip_if: You want naturalistic relationship drama or a conventional plot rhythm.

source_quotes.text: obsessed with the 4th wall breaks throughout. so fun and charming.
once things do start to click and you embrace that rhythm

summary: This is the accessible Godard pick for a group that wants cool, loose New Wave energy without committing to something too forbidding. One review calls it "effortlessly cool, charming and fun," especially if dancing and restless youth sound like the mood.
good_pick_if: You want stylish, short, cinephile-friendly mischief with a hangout feel.
maybe_skip_if: You need tight plotting or dislike casual New Wave detours.

source_quotes.text: effortlessly cool, charming and fun
the dance scene!!!! the louvre scene!!!!!!! ah that’s cinema

summary: A prickly relationship-drama pick for groups who like arguments that feel uncomfortably lived-in. "Make the story simple and the characters complicated" nails the appeal: the movie turns marriage talk into a jittery, sharp-edged pressure cooker.
good_pick_if: You want tense, talky adult drama with complicated people under pressure.
maybe_skip_if: You want comfort romance or creator baggage will derail the night.

source_quotes.text: Make the story simple and the characters complicated.
I loved the documentary style shooting and Mia farrow is just phenomenal

summary: Pick this when the room wants a lush, surreal mood piece more than a tidy story. "Each frame is a painting" is the cleanest pitch: Fellini turns domestic unease into color, costumes, dreams, and strange comic spectacle.
good_pick_if: You want lavish images, dream logic, and a movie people can interpret afterward.
maybe_skip_if: You need clean plot mechanics or grounded relationship drama.

source_quotes.text: Each frame is a painting
visually splendid, profound, memorable and nearly incomprehensible
